parts.t: Neighbourhood guide · City of Chilliwack · Ryder Lake
Ryder Lake is an MLS® sub-area name in the City of Chilliwack. The City doesn’t publish a boundary for it, and published municipal records list no street-by-street boundary in official sources.

The closest official descriptions are the City’s Greenspace Plan 2020, which lists Ryder Lake as numbered neighbourhood 47, and the City’s Mount Thom Park page, which places three of the park’s parking areas in Ryder Lake: Forester Road and Churchill Parkway, and Ross Road.
The 2040 Official Community Plan treated Ryder Lake as an upland area held as a medium-to-long-term development reserve.

Planning, zoning and flood

blocks.text: Planning and flood notes for Ryder Lake

parts.t: Plans, zoning and flood rules can be different for each lot.
The City of Chilliwack’s 2050 Official Community Plan, Official Community Plan Bylaw 2025, No. 5500, was adopted on December 16, 2025. It covers the whole city, including Ryder Lake.

Published municipal directories do not list a Ryder Lake neighbourhood plan separate from the Official Community Plan. Under the Chilliwack 2050 Official Community Plan, so verify parcel-level designation on the City of Chilliwack Webmap.

The 2040 plan’s policy was to maintain Ryder Lake as a medium to long term development reserve, keeping its rural estate density and preserving the upland area for development consideration beyond 2040.

The 2040 plan also called for limiting small-acreage rural and suburban residential development to the current zoning and discouraging rezoning for higher density. That plan has been replaced by the 2050 plan.
Hillside: Ryder Lake is one of the designated hillside and upland areas under Development Permit Area 2. A DPA2 permit is required before subdivision, construction, land clearing or earthworks.
The DPA2 guide says its objectives include reducing slope hazards, erosion and flooding, and making sure development responds to natural terrain and drainage patterns.

A DPA2 application needs a geotechnical report by a registered geotechnical engineer, with a hazard and slope assessment, setbacks, cut and fill, site stability, drainage and soil conditions. An environmental assessment and a hydrology report may also be required.
ALR: the 2040 policy supports agricultural activities on ALR parcels in Ryder Lake. ALR status is set parcel by parcel.

Flood: Published municipal directories do not list a flood document specific to Ryder Lake. The City’s Floodplain Regulation Bylaw No. 4519 applies to the floodplains the City designates, and Confirm on the municipal webmap whether any Ryder Lake parcel is inside one.

FAQ
Where is Ryder Lake?
The City doesn’t publish a boundary for Ryder Lake, and published municipal records list no street-by-street boundary in official sources.
The City’s Mount Thom Park page places three of the park’s parking areas in Ryder Lake: Forester Road and Churchill Parkway, and Ross Road.
Ask me if a specific address is in it.
How do I get around from Ryder Lake?
No BC Transit route serves Ryder Lake. The closest listed service is route 54 Promontory, which ends in the Promontory neighbourhood.
Published municipal records do not list new or planned transit lines for Ryder Lake.
Which school is in Ryder Lake?
No public school is located in Ryder Lake. SD33’s Long Range Facilities Plan 2021 to 2025 profiles 36 district sites and none is in Ryder Lake.
Use the official SD33 School Locator to confirm the catchment schools. Check an exact address with the
SD33 School Locator
What parks and library are near Ryder Lake?
Mount Thom Park, a 70-hectare wooded park with over 5 km of trails and three parking areas in Ryder Lake.
There is no library branch in Ryder Lake. The nearest are Sardis Library (5819 Tyson Road) and Chilliwack Library (45860 First Avenue).
What plan covers Ryder Lake?
The 2050 Official Community Plan covers the whole city, including Ryder Lake. There is no separate Ryder Lake neighbourhood plan.
The 2040 plan’s policy was to keep Ryder Lake as a medium to long term development reserve at its current rural estate density.
Is Ryder Lake a hillside or a floodplain area?
Ryder Lake is a designated hillside and upland area under Development Permit Area 2, so a DPA2 permit is required before subdivision, construction, land clearing or earthworks.
Published municipal directories do not list a flood document specific to Ryder Lake.
